title: Beyond the 956: Andy Taylor, founding Duran Duran guitarist, dies at 65
excerpt: Andy Taylor, the founding guitarist whose riffs powered Duran Duran's biggest hits, died Monday, November 23, 2026, at home surrounded by his family after a long battle with prostate cancer. He was 65.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Andy Taylor, the founding guitarist whose riffs powered Duran Duran's biggest hits and helped define the sound of the 1980s, has died at 65.

Taylor died peacefully at home on Monday, November 23, 2026, surrounded by his family, following a long and courageous battle with prostate cancer, according to a joint statement from his family and his former Duran Duran bandmates announced on Wednesday, November 25.

Born Andrew James Taylor on February 16, 1961, in Tynemouth, England, Taylor joined Duran Duran at the very beginning of the band's story. His guitar playing drove the songs that took the group around the world — including "Hungry Like the Wolf," "Rio," "The Reflex" and "A View to a Kill," the James Bond theme that became the first — and still only — 007 song to reach No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100. With Duran Duran, he won two Grammy Awards.

Taylor also co-founded the supergroup The Power Station, scoring a hit with "Some Like It Hot," and he reunited with the original five members of Duran Duran in the early 2000s for new music and tours.

Taylor was diagnosed with stage 4 prostate cancer in 2018. He revealed the diagnosis publicly in November 2022, when he was too ill to attend Duran Duran's induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame and frontman Simon Le Bon read a letter from him to the audience that night.

He is survived by his wife, Tracey; his children Georgina, Isabella, Bethany and Andrew; and his grandson, Albie. In lieu of flowers, the family has asked that donations be made in his name to Prostate Cancer UK.

Sources: Duran Duran official statement; People; Associated Press; Consequence.
